Family = "bedrock". Verify the image is real & maintained. Write it all as your final message.

I have everything I need. The image is confirmed real and actively maintained. Here is the ready-to-integrate recipe.

---

# Minecraft Bedrock — Nxeon Dockerized Game Server Recipe

Family = **`bedrock`**

## 1. Docker Image

- **Image:** `itzg/minecraft-bedrock-server`
- **Why:** The Bedrock counterpart to the `itzg/minecraft-server` (Java) image already used on Nxeon — same maintainer (`itzg`), same conventions, actively maintained (1.8k+ stars, continuous CI, `VERSION=LATEST` auto-downloads the current Bedrock Dedicated Server on start so version bumps are just a container restart). It maps env vars directly onto `server.properties`, which is exactly what game-config needs.
- **Verified URLs:**
  - Docker Hub: `https://hub.docker.com/r/itzg/minecraft-bedrock-server`
  - GitHub: `https://github.com/itzg/docker-minecraft-bedrock-server`

Note: Bedrock Dedicated Server is **UDP** (RakNet), unlike Java's TCP 25565 — the port MUST be published as `/udp`.

## 2. setupScript

```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && docker run -d --name bedrock \
  -e EULA=TRUE \
  -e SERVER_NAME="Nxeon Bedrock Server" \
  -e GAMEMODE=survival \
  -e DIFFICULTY=normal \
  -e LEVEL_NAME=Bedrock \
  -e MAX_PLAYERS=10 \
  -e ALLOW_CHEATS=false \
  -e VERSION=LATEST \
  -p 19132:19132/udp \
  -v /opt/bedrock:/data \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  itzg/minecraft-bedrock-server
```

Add `-p 19133:19133/udp` if IPv6 is offered (optional, see below).

## 3. Ports to forward

- `19132/udp` — **required** (IPv4, default game port, env `SERVER_PORT`)
- `19133/udp` — optional (IPv6, env `SERVER_PORT_V6`)

## 4. game-control

```
containerName: "bedrock"
configFile:    "/opt/bedrock/server.properties"
restart:       "docker restart bedrock"
```

The image expands the server and writes/reads `server.properties` inside `/data`, which is bind-mounted to `/opt/bedrock`, so the host path `/opt/bedrock/server.properties` is the live config file.

## 5. game-config FamilySchema

```js
{
  family: "bedrock",
  label: "Minecraft Bedrock",
  defaultVariant: "latest",
  variants: [
    { id: "latest",  label: "Latest",  description: "Always runs the newest Bedrock Dedicated Server release (auto-updates on restart)." },
    { id: "preview", label: "Preview", description: "Microsoft's Bedrock Preview build for early features and testing." }
  ],
  fields: [
    {
      key: "gamemode",
      label: "Game Mode",
      group: "Gameplay",
      type: "enum",
      default: "survival",
      options: [
        { value: "survival",  label: "Survival" },
        { value: "creative",  label: "Creative" },
        { value: "adventure", label: "Adventure" }
      ],
      phase: "live",
      help: "Default game mode for players joining the world."
    },
    {
      key: "difficulty",
      label: "Difficulty",
      group: "Gameplay",
      type: "enum",
      default: "normal",
      options: [
        { value: "peaceful", label: "Peaceful" },
        { value: "easy",     label: "Easy" },
        { value: "normal",   label: "Normal" },
        { value: "hard",     label: "Hard" }
      ],
      phase: "live",
      help: "World difficulty. Peaceful disables hostile mobs."
    },
    {
      key: "max-players",
      label: "Max Players",
      group: "Server",
      type: "int",
      default: 10,
      min: 1,
      max: 100,
      phase: "live",
      help: "Maximum number of simultaneous players."
    },
    {
      key: "allow-cheats",
      label: "Allow Cheats",
      group: "Gameplay",
      type: "bool",
      default: false,
      phase: "live",
      help: "Enables commands like /gamemode and /give for operators."
    },
    {
      key: "level-name",
      label: "World Name",
      group: "Server",
      type: "string",
      default: "Bedrock",
      phase: "deploy",
      help: "Name of the world folder. Changing this creates/loads a different world."
    }
  ]
}
```

Notes on mapping: the `key` values are the **real `server.properties` keys** (`gamemode`, `difficulty`, `max-players`, `allow-cheats`, `level-name`). The itzg image sets these via env vars `GAMEMODE`, `DIFFICULTY`, `MAX_PLAYERS`, `ALLOW_CHEATS`, `LEVEL_NAME`. game-control can either patch `/opt/bedrock/server.properties` directly then `docker restart bedrock`, or recreate the container with updated `-e` values. `level-name` is `phase:"deploy"` because switching worlds is disruptive; the rest are safely `phase:"live"` (edit properties + restart).

## 6. GamePlan tiers

Bedrock is very light — even a full survival server runs comfortably in 1–2 GB.

```js
[
  { name: "Bedrock Starter", ramMB: 1024, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 5,  slots: 5,  priceCents: 299 },
  { name: "Bedrock Plus",    ramMB: 2048, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 10, slots: 10, priceCents: 499, featured: true },
  { name: "Bedrock Pro",     ramMB: 3072, cpuCores: 2, diskGB: 20, slots: 20, priceCents: 799 },
  { name: "Bedrock Max",     ramMB: 4096, cpuCores: 2, diskGB: 40, slots: 40, priceCents: 1199 }
]
```

## 7. GAME_META

```js
{ name: "Minecraft Bedrock", tag: "Mobile & console cross-play" }
```
